subject: Post-call recap & next steps: NimbleHealth latency/throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps: NimbleHealth latency/throughput SLOs

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and clear asks so we can scope a pilot. High-level items we captured: 

- Target SLOs you called out: p95 end-to-end latency <= 400ms, but you emphasized first-byte streaming feel should be ~200ms for UX.
- Peak/sustained traffic: peak ~120 QPS, sustained ~40 QPS. Typical per-request concurrency ~2. Median prompt length ~100-150 tokens; some longer transcripts (~700 tokens) in edge cases.
- Streaming is required for partial transcript updates (chat-like experience).
- Compliance: workload will require HIPAA controls; you'll follow up with security questionnaire.

How Redwood can hit those SLOs (summary):
- Continuous batching with a low max-batch-delay (10-30ms) to reduce token-cost without harming first-byte latency.
- Prefix/KV caching for common templates and standard prompts — should reduce token generation by ~20-35% on conversational flows.
- Quantization profile: recommend trying int8 quant (q8 or q5-like profile) for the primary model to cut cost ~35-60% depending on throughput and accuracy tolerance.
- Model variants: use a low-latency 13B quantized model for interactive sessions and fallback to a smaller 7B variant for bulk processing or lower-priority batch jobs.
- Dedicated capacity recommendation for pilot: 2x GPUs (reserved) to meet peak concurrency with predictable latency; hosted burst model also possible but has tradeoffs for guaranteed p95.

Attachments: I attached an initial SLO proposal and a rough cost sketch (slo-proposal-nimble.pdf).

Next steps I'd suggest:
1) You confirm the peak/sustained numbers above and whether 120 QPS is a firm peak.
2) We run a 2-week pilot: Redwood provides a dedicated test pool + telemetry, we run your representative prompt set and streaming workload.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security (30–45m) next week — please propose times.
4) I’ll produce a short estimate for monthly cost under two options (dedicated vs hosted) and a configuration that targets your $15k/mo guidance.

Let me know if I missed anything. Happy to sync with your infra/security and procurement as soon as you say the word.

— Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: slo-proposal-nimble.pdf (proposal summary, 3 pages)
From: Devon Park <devon@nimblehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimble Health Procurement <procurement@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 09:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: NimbleHealth latency/throughput SLOs

Thanks, Sergio — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak (120 QPS) is what our demo can hit; production peak may be higher during flash events but for now planning for 120. Sustained 40 QPS is accurate.
- Concurrency per active user is effectively 2 (one streaming session + occasional side request).
- Typical prompt sizes: 120 tokens median; we have a small subset (5-7% of requests) that are 400–800 tokens.
- Streaming is required for the first-byte/partial updates. UX team wants sub-200ms first-byte at p95 if possible.

Questions: 
1) How does continuous batching interact with the streaming requirement? Will batching add unacceptable first-byte latency?
2) Any concerns about caching overhead for PHI/HIPAA data? We need to ensure any cache is encrypt-at-rest and can be flushed per-tenant.
3) Our procurement target is to get pilots under $15k/month if we can. Is that a realistic starter configuration?

I attached a small sample traffic RPM extract — nimble-rpm.csv — to help with the estimate. Can you do a quick cost sketch back to procurement? Also include a security contact for the questionnaire.

— Devon Park
Head of Product, Nimble Health
devon@nimblehealth.com
Attachment: nimble-rpm.csv (sample request-per-minute traffic)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: NimbleHealth latency/throughput SLOs

Great questions — quick answers and a practical config we can pilot: 

1) Continuous batching + streaming: continuous batching works by aggregating small requests while honoring a max-batch-delay. For streaming-first-byte constraints we recommend a max-batch-delay of 10–20ms and a small batch size target (2–8). That preserves first-byte latency while still harvesting batching efficiency for tail tokens. We can tune this during the test run.

2) Caching + PHI: Redwood supports per-tenant KV caching with AES-256 encryption at rest, and caches can be invalidated on demand. For HIPAA workloads we recommend tenant-scoped caches with strict TTLs and an explicit flush API; we’ll include this in the security questionnaire response.

3) Cost target: a starter pilot that aims for your $15k/mo is feasible if we accept a mix of quantized models + careful batching and a capped reserved capacity footprint. Rough estimate scenarios (very rough):
   - Hosted burst (no reserved): $18k–$28k/mo (higher variability)
   - Dedicated pilot (2x A10-class GPUs, int8 quant primary model, caching): $9k–$13k/mo depending on observed cache hit-rate and batch efficiency.

Model recommendation for pilot: redwood-llama-13b-quant-q8 (interactive) with redwood-llama-7b-quant-q5 as fallback for bulk jobs. We’ll supply an alternative lower-latency 6–8B variant if the first-byte SLA needs tighter guarantees.

Next steps I can take this week:
• Produce a 2-page config + cost sheet and a test plan (I attached rough-estimate-20260413.xlsx).
• Set up a 45-minute technical deep-dive with our infra lead (suggest Wed/Thu next week). Please loop in your security/infrastructure lead and procurement.

If you confirm the pilot window and who from your team will join the deep-dive I’ll lock calendar invites and provision a test endpoint.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai
Attachments: rough-estimate-20260413.xlsx
